title: Efficient Edge Vision Transformer Accelerator with Decoupled Chunk Attention and Hybrid Computing-In-Memory
problem: Vision Transformers suffer from quadratic self-attention complexity, making them slow and resource-intensive for dense pixel-level predictions on edge devices; pyramid ViT architecture creates unbalanced workloads and poor hardware utilization.
motivation: ViTs are emerging foundation models for edge vision tasks like autonomous driving; efficient edge deployment requires addressing attention complexity and workload imbalance.
method: Proposes decoupled chunk attention (DCA) in pipelined form to reduce off-chip memory access; combines SRAM-based computing-in-memory with RRAM nonvolatile storage; bit/element two-way-reconfigurable CIM macros adapt to varied pyramid ViT block sizes; fusion scheduling balances workload and minimizes intermediate memory.
key_novelty: Decoupled chunk attention mechanism with pipelined execution and hybrid CIM-RRAM architecture featuring reconfigurable bit/element-level computation macros.
contributions: Decoupled chunk attention (DCA) for pipelined off-chip memory reduction
Hybrid SRAM-CIM and RRAM storage architecture eliminating extensive off-chip access
Bit/element two-way-reconfigurable CIM macros for pyramid ViT workload adaptation
Fusion scheduling for workload balancing and intermediate memory minimization
18.5×-217.1× speedup with 1.7×-7.4× memory access reduction and 1.8× energy efficiency gain
limitations: Evaluation on specific dense prediction tasks; generalization to other ViT-based applications not discussed.
primary_theme: Hybrid CIM-RRAM ViT accelerator with decoupled chunk attention and reconfigurable macros
